pr_title: 2D: Combine texture state to batch more subsequent commands together
pr_body: This PR builds on #92797, to improve the 2D renderer, such that it can combine commands that change texture state, allowing for more cases to be rendered as a single draw call. Using driver limits, the current implementation will support up to 64 textures in a single batch. Additionally, samplers have been moved back to an array for canvas rendering, so batching can dynamically address the default samplers like `SAMPLER_NEAREST_CLAMP`. 3 additional sampler states are supported that are not available in the default samplers, such as mirror-repeat, bringing the per batch to a maximum of 15 sampler states. Another important change in this PR is to move the `specular_shininess` to `PushConstant` state, allowing the field to be used for #97058. # Bugfixes - As noted in [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/97586#issuecomment-2380882016), fixes #97586 for the forward+ renderer, but not compatibility - Closes #97593 which is a forward+ issue only - Fixes #97774 - Fixes #98005 # Background One benefactor of this improvement is text rendering, which changes texture state to render effects such as shadows. A demonstration of that was [a comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/92797#issuecomment-2309051165) by @passivstar. With this PR, we can see that the number of draw calls was reduced from 40,332 down to 4, which an associated frame-rate increase: | master | This PR | |:---- |:---- | | 40 fps | 400+ fps | | 40332 draw calls | 4 draw calls | | | | Cases where unique textures are used for sprites may also benefit from this PR. To demonstrate this, I modified @Calinou's test project to draw 10,000 sprites, from [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/92797#pullrequestreview-2100153431), to alternate between two sprites using different textures. | master | This PR | |:---- |:---- | | 214 fps | 469 fps | | 10004 draw calls | 1 draw call | | | | > [!NOTE] > > Also shows that the label is combined into the same draw call, so the entire scene is rendered in a single draw call.
pr_comments: @clayjohn I have not converted the SAMPLERS back to an array, but if we did, we could use that for sampler state dynamically, rather than a separate array. I would extend the length from 12 to 16, so that the 2D renderer could add up to 4 unique sampler states per draw call, that aren't available in the default list. That is probably MIRROR_REPEAT, which isn't available in the default sampler states.
Also note that this PR will help with moving to batching multiple command types together.

Using @clayjohn's words, with this _one simple trick_, frame rate for his pathological test case jumped from 25 fps to 45 fps on my M1. 

The improvement was to remove all the allocations building the `RD::Uniform` arrays each batch. I dropped the number of **transient** allocations from 2.9 million for a 3-second window:

![CleanShot 2024-10-05 at 06 15 17@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24923d81-9e4b-440b-8265-ff89e3534a48)

to 8,796 over the same periond

![CleanShot 2024-10-05 at 06 15 32@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/046ba9a4-69cf-473d-926c-0bba533a9a37)

We can see that removing the `append_id` gained us 40% back on the `_render_batch` function, with this before snapshot:

![CleanShot 2024-10-05 at 06 31 37@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/254b58f4-bece-4ee7-bbd5-d8b86556f5ac)

An this after:

![CleanShot 2024-10-05 at 06 31 44@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/995c2db1-54a8-4a41-b7c7-7c54f5c4ce38)

Next I want to focus on the `get_cache` call, as I think we can optimise for our use case in the 2D renderer. It isn't critical for this PR, but we can see that if we focus on just the `_render_batch` call, 80% of the usage is charged to the `get_cache` call:

![CleanShot 2024-10-05 at 06 36 47@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/949a660d-e333-4b12-91b5-a9bd7fa7154d)

It has to be very generic and compare _all the uniform state_, including the binding, type, number of RIDs and if the RIDs are the same. We can do better for these two uniforms in the canvas renderer I believe

@Calinou / @clayjohn regarding **Sprite rendering (1 unique texture per sprite)** test: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97340#pullrequestreview-2374632529

The problem is that the uniform set cache is being thrashed (I knew that would be a problem with the right conditions). Bindless textures would be really nice…

Some options:

1. Allow the cache size to be configurable, so that a user can adjust for their specific scenario. Its not perfect, but would give the user a simple option
2. Provide an option to choose to the batch mode, and include single-texture batching, which for a game with 100s or thousands of unique (or dynamic) sprites, might be a better fit
3. Do both

> [!NOTE]
>
> 1. is easy, and I think we _should_ do it anyway, as that gives the user a way to address cache thrashing. Cache invalidations (or perhaps uniform set creation count) would be worth adding to the monitors / visual profiler too.

Whilst investigating, I've identified an issue that if the texture is changed:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e2c6daf7eff6e0b7e2e8d967e95a9ad56e948231/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp#L581-L597

`TextureStorageRD` invalidate caches; however, it won't invalidate the cache in the 2D renderer. 

Another issue is that if a texture is freed, we would need to invalidate the 2D renderer caches. However, it is unclear if this is taken care of by the `uniform_set_invalidation_callback`, when a texture is freed? We subscribe to this for invalidating the cache.

**EDIT**: Yes, it does appear that if a texture is freed, the associated uniform set will be freed, as it is a direct dependency. I do see invalidation callbacks being called when a texture is freed. Texture updates are still an issue.

We would need to add a notification / callback so the 2D renderer can subscribe and invalidate any uniform sets when the texture is changed.

We may still have to limit the size of the cache, as draw order changes might still generate an unbounded number of uniform sets if the set of bound sprites for a given batch does not exist. Normally, the batching attempts to put the same texture in the same array slot, to reuse the same uniform set.
I can confirm the cache is invalidated when textures are freed, so we just need to address the _changed_ issue.

Another pathological case is that if the ordering of nodes changes regularly, and the number of textures is high, it will result in uniform set churn. Not sure if this is a realistic scenario, as any solution we introduce is likely to perform poorly is some cases.

I added a timer to @Calinou's `unique` test case, and a 2D node named `Sprites` to add the 10,000 sprites:

```gdscript
func _on_timer_timeout() -> void:
	var node = sprites.get_child(0)
	sprites.remove_child(node)
	node.queue_free()
	
	sprites.get_children().shuffle()
	
	var sprite := $Sprite2D.duplicate()
	var tex := GradientTexture2D.new()
	tex.width = 1
	tex.height = 1
	sprite.texture = tex
	sprite.position.x = randf_range(0, 1152)
	sprite.position.y = randf_range(0, 648)
	sprites.add_child(sprite)
```

Here are my recommendations (besides the bug fix):

1. Add a project setting to disable texture batching and fall back to the alternate, which would address cases where there are high numbers of unique sprites and / or lots of churn in the node hierarchy[^1]
2. Add a project setting to configure the max size of the uniform set cache

[^1]: The churn is ok if there aren't huge numbers of unique sprite textures or the number of sprite textures is < `texture_batch_size`, which is the size of the texture array in `canvas.glsl`

This might be the same problem as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98288 Basically non-uniform access into a array can cause issues. We need to double check that all array indices appear as uniform to the shader compiler

_edit: confirmed The following diff is enough to fix things on an AMD 6900 XT:_

```
diff --git a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/canvas_uniforms_inc.glsl b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/canvas_uniforms_inc.glsl
index 2f57f69654..9db7b407dc 100644
--- a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/canvas_uniforms_inc.glsl
+++ b/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/canvas_uniforms_inc.glsl
@@ -176,6 +176,8 @@ transforms;

 /* SET3: Texture */

+#extension GL_EXT_nonuniform_qualifier : require
+
 layout(set = 3, binding = 0) uniform texture2D texture_array[BATCH_MAX_TEXTURES];

 #define SAMPLER_LINEAR_CLAMP material_samplers[1]
@@ -187,10 +189,10 @@ layout(set = 3, binding = 0) uniform texture2D texture_array[BATCH_MAX_TEXTURES]
 /// - 3 dynamic samplers
 layout(set = 3, binding = 1) uniform sampler material_samplers[15];

-#define color_texture texture_array[BATCH_COLOR_INDEX]
-#define normal_texture texture_array[BATCH_NORMAL_INDEX]
-#define specular_texture texture_array[BATCH_SPECULAR_INDEX]
-#define texture_sampler material_samplers[BATCH_SAMPLER_INDEX]
+#define color_texture texture_array[nonuniformEXT(BATCH_COLOR_INDEX)]
+#define normal_texture texture_array[nonuniformEXT(BATCH_NORMAL_INDEX)]
+#define specular_texture texture_array[nonuniformEXT(BATCH_SPECULAR_INDEX)]
+#define texture_sampler material_samplers[nonuniformEXT(BATCH_SAMPLER_INDEX)]

 layout(set = 3, binding = 2, std430) restrict readonly buffer DrawData {
        InstanceData data[];
```

However, outside of MacOS, we don't do any validation to ensure that non uniform access is available.

> Whilst investigating, I've identified an issue that if the texture is changed:

@clayjohn turns out this isn't a bug, and we're all good!

1. We clear out the `texture_info_map` each iteration, and fetch them again from `TextureStorageRD`, so any changes will be received on the next frame
2. the cache is keyed by the specific texture RIDs, so the code will create a new entry in the cache if those were changed.
3. The dependency management will also inform the cache of invalidated uniform set RIDS. If the RID of a texture the uniform set depends on is freed, the existing code will free the uniform set:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e2c6daf7eff6e0b7e2e8d967e95a9ad56e948231/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp#L169-L175

# Performance Summary

I tested on 4 devices:
1. A desktop PC with a relatively strong GPU, but an outdated CPU
2. A mid range laptop with a decent CPU, but a weak GPU
3. An older flagship phone
4. A new flagship phone

The only device where this PR is a consistent win in all cases is on the desktop computer where the extra GPU cost is minimal and doesn't impact the overall frame rate. The other cases (where an integrated GPU is used), the impact on GPU performance appears to outweigh the gains to CPU performance in most cases.

This PR is a huge win for shadows text batching in all cases, but in non-pathological cases the results are less clear. 

Overall, the places where it is an improvement it is a huge improvement, and where it is worse, it isn't much worse (and the negative GPU performance can likely be mitigated to an extent with further profiling

## Demo scenes

**Isometric**
This is the [Isometric2D](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/2d/isometric) demo project without modification. 

In general, this is a GPU-bound scene due to the already low number of draw calls and the very high number of lights with shadows. 

**Platformer6X**
This is the [2D platformer](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/2d/platformer) demo modified to have the "Level" scene copied 6 times.

Physics ends up taking a significant amount of the frame time here.

**drawcalltest**
This is a worst case scenario test project. It does 10,001 draw calls and force disables any batching. It is expected that this PR would perform worse under these conditions.
[drawcalltest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17526437/drawcalltest.zip)

This test should not be treated the same as the others, it displays worst-case performance, but is extremely unrealistic. 

**Shadowedtext**
This is the MRP provided by passivestar earlier: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/92797#issuecomment-2309051165

Its just one big label with a ton of text using a shadowed font (which previously broke batching)

## Results

CPU: Ryzen 5 3600
GPU: RX 6900 XT

**Isometric demo: 800 FPS -> 850 FPS**
**PlatformerX6: 100 FPS -> 150 FPS**
note: highly variable due to physics costs
before: 30 FPS - 200 FPS
after: 70 FPS - 310 FPS

issue_context.title: Vertex colors are assigned incorrectly in quadrilaterals drawn using CommandPrimitive
issue_context.body: ### Tested versions Master as of writing: v4.4.dev.custom_build [76a135926] Regression after #92797 (bisected) ### System information Godot v4.4.dev (a657ea42f) - Windows 10.0.22631 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3699) - AMD Ryzen 9 7950X 16-Core Processor (32 Threads) ### Issue description Quadrilaterals drawn using CommandPrimitive (`RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_primitive()`, antialiasing etc.) assign the provided vertex colors incorrectly after #92797 in the RD-renderers. More specifically, the second constructed triangle (top left, bottom right, bottom left in the first image) uses the colors indexed at 0, 1 and 2, when it should use 0, 2 and 3. ```gdscript func _draw() -> void: var uvs: PackedVector2Array = [Vector2.ZERO, Vector2.RIGHT, Vector2.ONE, Vector2.DOWN] var colors: PackedColorArray = [Color.WHITE, Color.RED, Color.GREEN, Color.BLUE] var points: PackedVector2Array = uvs.duplicate() for i: int in points.size(): points[i] *= 500 points[i] += Vector2(50, 50) draw_primitive(points, colors, uvs) ``` Incorrect antialiasing of line (drawn with scale 10 to blow out the feather size): Compatibility for reference: ### Steps to reproduce ↕ ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [primitivevertexcolors.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17175703/primitivevertexcolors.zip)
